newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Too early to go short, Brussels bourse traders say.
newsitem.headline: Too early to go short, Brussels bourse traders say.

text.p: Investors should stay with it, Brussels bourse traders recommended on Wednesday after the Bel-20 share index hit another record close.

"Sentiment is quite good, sometimes a bit irrational, but everybody is still buying and you have to go with the flow," a trader said. The dollar remained strong and official interest rates low, so the market would continue to advance.

With the U.S. policy-making FOMC widely expected to hold key rates steady after its two-day meeting ending later on Wednesday, "the party can go on tomorrow." He added it was impossible to say at what Bel-20 level the rally would end.
"I do not dare go short in this market," he added.
The Bel-20 index ended at a record 2,444.93 points, up 1.51 percent on the day, but off an intraday high of 2,452.97.
The index has been advancing again after pausing from June 13 to 27, as it hit 2,400 points.
Another trader said he did not expect news of unchanged U.S. interest rates to lift the barometer to 2,500 points, the next big figure and psychological hurdle for the market.
The bourse was overbought and expensive and valuations were becoming such that "for every Belgian share you can find a nice alternative abroad," he said.
Features of the day were retailer Colruyt, up 1,675 francs at 19,875, and insurer Royale Belge, 350 francs higher at 10,975.
Royale Belge, bank BBL in which it has a share, and holding company GBL which controls part of the insurer, stood out again on a flare-up of talk of a Royale Belge sale to Dutch financial group ING.

The talk refocused interest on a BBL merger or takeover by Royale Belge's potential buyer. In the wake of the Royale Belge rise, insurer Fortis AG benefitted from talk of consolidation in the European insurance sector as a whole.

One trader said the interest was sparked by news French financial giant AXA-UAP -- Royale Belge's parent -- restructured some of its UK holdings, tying up loose ends left by last year's merger between AXA and UAP, which created the world's second-largest life insurer.
He said the move was seen as a precursor to AXA-UAP tidying up its Belgian interests.
Another trader said there had been heavy buyers in Royale Belge. Volume was 25,043 shares on Wednesday.

He said players had been arbitraging between insurers Fortis AG and Amev, the Dutch arm of the Fortis group. Fortis AG closed at 7,690 francs, up 150 on the day. Amev gained one guilder at 89.00 guilders.

Retailer Colruyt continued its spell in the sun, helped by fresh Belgian and Anglo-Saxon broker recommendations, market praise for recently released 1996/97 results and unyielding speculation the company stood to gain from a possible sale or bourse listing of part of its computer operations.
One trader said the share's relative illiquidity meant smallish deals could have large impacts.
